title: Vulcanair is founded, as did airline company Minerva Airlines.
text: Vulcanair is an Italian aircraft manufacturer based in Casoria, near Naples.

title: 11 people die in the Secondigliano district, in Naples, due to the Secondigliano tragedy.
text: Secondigliano is a quarter in the north of Naples, Italy. It is part of the 7th municipality of Naples, along with the neighbourhoods of Miano and San Pietro a Patierno.

title: Murder of Nada Cella.
text: Nada Cella was a 25-year-old Italian woman who was murdered at her place of work on the morning of 6 May 1996 in Chiavari, in the metropolitan city of Genoa. The crime, known in Italy as the delitto di via Marsala has remained unsolved for 30 years.

title: a little girl named Angela Celentano, who disappeared near Naples, the little girl was never found again.
text: Angela Celentano is an Italian missing person. Her disappearance occurred on 10 August 1996 on Monte Faito in the municipality of Castellammare di Stabia, in the province of Naples.

title: Buonvicino massacre.
text: The Buonvicino massacre was a crime committed on 19 November 1996 in Buonvicino, in the province of Cosenza, Italy, by the Carabiniere Alfredo Valente against his wife and her family, for reasons of jealousy. Valente was convicted of murdering six family members and was released from prison in 2021.

title: 1995–96 Serie A (ice hockey) season
text: The 1995–96 Serie A season was the 62nd season of the Serie A, the top level of ice hockey in Italy. Nine teams participated in the league, and HC Bozen won the championship by defeating HC 24 Milan in the final.

title: 1996 San Marino Grand Prix
text: The 1996 San Marino Grand Prix was a Formula One motor race held on 5 May 1996 at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari, Imola, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. It was the fifth round of the 1996 Formula One season.

title: 1996 Italian motorcycle Grand Prix
text: The 1996 Italian motorcycle Grand Prix was the fifth race of the 1996 Grand Prix motorcycle racing season. It took place on 26 May 1996 at the Mugello Circuit.

title: Italy at the 1996 Summer Olympics
text: Italy competed at the 1996 Summer Olympics in Atlanta, United States. 340 competitors, 236 men and 104 women, took part in 172 events in 27 sports.

title: Italy at the 1996 Summer Paralympics
text: 79 athletes from Italy competed at the 1996 Summer Paralympics in Atlanta, United States.

title: “Gangsta's Paradise” by Coolio featuring L.V.
text: "Gangsta's Paradise" is a song by American rapper Coolio featuring American singer L.V. It was released as a single on August 1, 1995, by Tommy Boy, Warner Bros., and MCA Records. The song was written by the artists alongside producer Doug Rasheed, with additional credits going to Stevie Wonder for the interpolation of his 1976 song "Pastime Paradise".

title: “Children” by Robert Miles
text: "Children" is an instrumental composition by Italian composer Robert Miles. It was first released in Italy in January 1995 as part of the EP Soundtracks on Joe T. Vannelli's DBX label, but it did not chart.

title: “La terra dei cachi” by Elio e le Storie Tese
text: "La terra dei cachi" is a 1996 single by Elio e le Storie Tese. Thanks to a live performance of this song, which represents a humorous take on Italian lifestyle, Elio e le Storie Tese acquired national notoriety by achieving a second-place finish at the Sanremo Music Festival 1996.
listen: La terra dei cachi Elio e le Storie Tese

title: “They Don't Care About Us” by Michael Jackson
text: "They Don't Care About Us" is a protest song by the American singer Michael Jackson, released on April 8, 1996, in the UK, and April 23 in the US. It was the fourth single from Jackson's ninth album, HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I. The initial release contained ethnic slurs, triggering accusations of antisemitism.
listen: They Don't Care About Us Michael Jackson

title: “California Love” by 2pac
text: "California Love" is a song by American rapper 2Pac featuring fellow American rapper Dr. Dre and American musician Roger Troutman.

title: “Più bella cosa” by Eros Ramazzotti
text: "Più bella cosa" is an Italian language song written by singer Eros Ramazzotti, with Claudio Guidetti, Maurizio Fabrizio and Adelio Cogliati, and performed by Ramazzotti in February 1996, as a first single and pre-release from his album Dove c'è musica ("Where There's Music") that came out on 13 May of that year. The song is dedicated to the Swiss model Michelle Hunziker, Ramazzotti's girlfriend at the time.

title: “Fastlove”
text: "Fastlove" is a song by the English singer-songwriter George Michael, released on 22 April 1996 as the second single from his third album, Older. It was written by Michael, Patrice Rushen, Freddie Washington and Terri McFaddin and produced by Michael and Jon Douglas.

title: “Don't Stop Movin'” by Livin' Joy
text: "Don't Stop Movin'" is a song by Italian electronic dance music group Livin' Joy. It was released on 3 June 1996 by MCA Records.

title: “Fable” by Robert Miles
text: "Fable" is a song by Italian musician Robert Miles, released in May 1996 as the second single from his debut album, Dreamland. The song features uncredited vocals from Fiorella Quinn.

title: “Summer Is Crazy” by Alexia
text: "Summer Is Crazy" is a song by Italian singer-songwriter Alexia, released in May 1996, by DWA Records and Dance Pool, as the second single from her debut studio album, Fan Club. Co-written by Alexia with Roberto Zanetti, who also produced it, the song was very successful, reaching number one on the Italian singles chart.

title: “Killing Me Softly” by Fugees
text: "Killing Me Softly with His Song" is a song composed by Charles Fox with lyrics by Norman Gimbel. The lyrics were written in collaboration with Lori Lieberman after she was inspired by a Don McLean performance in late 1971.
wiki: Killing Me Softly with His Song

title: “What Goes Around Comes Around” by Bob Marley
text: Robert Nesta Marley was a Jamaican reggae singer, songwriter, and guitarist. Considered one of the pioneers of the genre, he was renowned for his distinctive vocal and songwriting style.
listen: What Goes Around Comes Around Bob Marley

title: “Stranger in Moscow” by Michael Jackson
text: "Stranger in Moscow" is a song by American singer and songwriter Michael Jackson from his ninth studio album, HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I. The song was released as the fifth and final single in Europe in September 1996 by Epic Records, with a UK-release on November 4, 1996.

title: “Born Slippy” by Underworld
text: "Born Slippy .NUXX" is a song by the British electronic music group Underworld. It was first released as the B-side to another track, "Born Slippy", in May 1995.

title: “One and One” by Robert Miles and Maria Nayler
text: "One and One" is a song written by Billy Steinberg, Rick Nowels and Marie-Claire D'Ubaldo. The song was first recorded by Edyta Górniak.
